newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s end with only marginal losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s end with only marginal losses.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor's 500 futures ended a choppy day with only marginal losses due to a rebound in some technology stocks, traders and analysts said.
June Nasdaq 100s closed more than 21 points higher, reflecting the resilient rally in technology-related stocks. The rally helped lift S&Ps off session lows, they said.

"Tech stocks are just feeding off the exuberance in IBM," one S&P futures trader said. IBM's first-quarter earnings were higher than expected and helped propel technology stocks, many of which languished during Tuesday's S&P rally, higher.
The strength in technology stocks, however, could not pull June S&Ps into positive territory at the close.
The contract spent most of the day caught in a battle between the tech stocks and the steadily eroding U.S. bond market, which softened in the afternoon.
For most of the day, the weight of the U.S. bonds overshadowed the rally in tech stocks, traders said.
At one point, June S&Ps briefly bounced through 782.50, the 50-percent retracement level from the all-time high of 827.80 on February 19 and last Monday's 4-1/2-month low at 736.70.
Howver, June S&Ps also had to contend with technical factors that pointed to a downside correction after Tuesday's 17-point rally.
"There are a lot of bullets out there," one trader said about the whipsaw nature of Wednesday's pit trade.
Arbitrage sell programs at about 3.30 points over cash were noted in the afternoon. Fair value stands at 4.30 points, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 5.30 points.
"The volume was moderate, but it was very choppy and you really had to stay on your toes," said Kurt Schultz, a floor analyst at Refco Inc.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were down 0.55 at 780.20, KCBT Value Lines were down 0.30 at 688.40, NYSE Composites were off 1.20 at 408.00, Nikkeis were up 100 at 18,790, Midcap 400s were 0.90 higher at 253.60, Nasdaq 100s were 21.25 higher at 847.75 and Russell 2000s were 0.70 higher at 341.00. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
